newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly higher, volumes up.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly higher, volumes up.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly higher Thursday, after wide intraday swings in gold and silver, on very high volume in COMEX gold trading.

"Fund short covering and local buying drove gold higher intraday, and silver was dragged up as a result, but it all fell apart again around $330.00, leaving little net change on the day in gold," Pioneer Futures analyst Scott Meyers said.
"The bottom line is precious metals are still weak, and rallies should be sold into," he said.
COMEX August gold settled unchanged at $323.80 an ounce, masking the intraday volatility.

Support in August gold held early in the day just above $322.00, a level which had provided resistance for most of the previous two week, and locals took the opportunity to reverse and go long, while funds covered short positions and rolled into the December contract, traders said.
But around the $330.00 level, which had proved to be resistance earlier this week, locals and funds turned sellers into the close.
Volume boosted by heavy rollovers from the August into the December contract. August gold's first notice day is next Thursday, July 31.
Estimated total volume in COMEX gold was 95,000 lots, the third highest volume day this year.
But COMEX gold open interest rose Wednesday by 1,576 lots to 206,207 contracts, after fund shortcovering resulted in a sharp decline earlier this week from 18 month highs at 222,069 lots.

The intraday volatility has lifted the average range for the day over $5.00 an ounce this week, based on a standard 10-day average true-range indicator, while 20-day historical volatility climbed to 17 percent from below 10 percent at the beginning of July.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted around $324.00/50, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $321.95 and the New York close Wednesday around $322.75/25.

Gold prices have been consolidating in the past two weeks after hitting a 12 year low in early July around $314.00 an ounce, following confirmation of a sale of 167 tonnes of gold by the Australian central bank.
But news overnight brought further evidence of likely mine production cutbacks as a result of the price slide.
Anglo-American Corp of South Africa Ltd's gold division, Anglogold, said the low gold price necessitated a review of all financially marginal shafts at its Free State Consolidated Gold Mines Ltd.
Anglogold said five shafts at Freegold, the world's largest gold mine, were identified at the end of the previous quarter as being in financial trouble.
Meanwhile, COMEX September silver ended down 1.5 cents at $4.280 an ounce, after again running into resistance around $4.40, and being dragged back down by the action in gold.

But NYMEX October platinum ended up $4.00 at $412.20 an ounce, with the contract's five-day moving-average climing back above its 21-day and 55-day average this week, signalling a possible resumption of the uptrend seen earlier this year.

The October/January platinum spread widened out to a high for the two contracts at $11.00 an ounce, emphasizing the ongoing backwardation in the forward price structure, despite the resumption of Russian platinum group metal (PGM) exports this month.
The October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread soared to $85.00 an ounce, a new high for the two contracts.

"Although most of the early 1980's saw platinum trade with a $30-$50 premium to gold, it is worthwhile to compare the current economic scenario to the situation in the late 1980's, when platinum typically maintained a $100-$150 premium over gold," Platinum Guild International analyst Aran Murphy said.
"Both periods displayed characteristics of strong economic growth and low inflation, relative economic stability, and concern over near-term PGM supplies," he said.

NYMEX September palladium ended up $6.00 at $185.50 an ounce, with the September/December spread climbing back to $10.00 an ounce, the level seen in early June, just before the resumption of Russian PGM exports.
In overnight news, Japanese traders said they expected the first Russian platinum shipments in six months would reach Japan by Monday next week. The first palladium shipments arrived last week.

Meanwhile, Russian metal export agency Almaz, was again seen offering palladium in the spot market in Europe overnight, but traders said the problem was that not enough Russian metal was being supplied to meet pent up demand.
